about: Part B: new briefs, run end to end through each setup. Answers stand in for the question round. Checks are what the jury verifies in the final PRD; each is a concrete, checkable claim drawn from the knowledge pack or the answers.

briefs.brief: On CO-197 denials, the specialist must attach an existing authorization reference before resubmitting, and lines with no authorization reference must go to the authorization desk instead of being resubmitted.

answers.question: What counts as an authorization reference?
answers.answer: A non-empty AUTH-#### id; free text does not count.

answers.question: Can the specialist resubmit without one?
answers.answer: No. The line is routed to the authorization desk for a retro request.

answers.question: Does this change any other denial code?
answers.answer: No. Only CO-197 lines are affected.

checks: The CO-197 next action is copied exactly: 'Attach the authorization reference if one exists. Otherwise route to the authorization desk for a retro request.'
A CO-197 line with no AUTH-#### reference cannot be resubmitted and is routed to the authorization desk.
Free text in the authorization field does not count as a reference.
No other denial code's behaviour changes.
Every acceptance criterion's outcome can be observed by a test.
Nothing is presented as agreed that the decisions did not say; any such choice is flagged under open questions as a proposal needing sign-off.
No feature beyond the brief and the decisions (for example an audit log, an override, or a notification) is added unless it is flagged as a proposal.
AUTH-123 (three digits) and auth-1234 (lower case) do not count as authorization references.

briefs.brief: On CO-16 denials, the specialist must see which claim element the remark code says is missing before the claim can be resubmitted.

answers.question: Where does the missing element come from?
answers.answer: From the remark code on the remit; the product does not guess.

answers.question: Who works CO-16 lines?
answers.answer: The biller, as resubmissions.

answers.question: What if the remark code is unknown?
answers.answer: The line shows the code as unmapped and resubmission stays blocked.

checks: The CO-16 next action is copied exactly: 'Correct the missing element named by the remark and resubmit the claim.'
The missing element is named from the remark code, never inferred.
An unknown remark code is shown as unmapped and blocks resubmission.
The biller, not the front desk, works CO-16 resubmissions.
Every acceptance criterion's outcome can be observed by a test.
Nothing is presented as agreed that the decisions did not say; any such choice is flagged under open questions as a proposal needing sign-off.
No feature beyond the brief and the decisions (for example an audit log, an override, or a notification) is added unless it is flagged as a proposal.
When the remark code is known but names no claim element, resubmission stays blocked rather than letting the biller choose an element.

briefs.brief: The denial workqueue must sort appealable denials by days remaining to the filing deadline and label each row overdue, urgent, soon, or comfortable.

answers.question: Where do the bands start?
answers.answer: Urgent is 0 to 14 days, soon is 15 to 45 days, comfortable is more than 45 days, and past the deadline is overdue.

answers.question: Which date is the deadline?
answers.answer: Date of service plus 90 days, per Northwind Health timely filing.

answers.question: Where do rows with no deadline go?
answers.answer: They are labelled missing and sort before comfortable rows.

checks: The deadline is the date of service plus 90 days.
Band boundaries are exactly: overdue below 0 days, urgent 0-14, soon 15-45, comfortable above 45.
Any worked date example in the document is arithmetically correct.
Rows with no deadline are labelled missing and never shown as comfortable.
Patient-responsibility (PR-1) lines are not in the appealable list.
Nothing is presented as agreed that the decisions did not say; any such choice is flagged under open questions as a proposal needing sign-off.
No feature beyond the brief and the decisions (for example an audit log, an override, or a notification) is added unless it is flagged as a proposal.
A row exactly 14 days out is urgent, exactly 15 days is soon, exactly 45 days is soon, and exactly 46 days is comfortable.

briefs.brief: PR-1 deductible lines must go to a patient-responsibility group and must never offer an appeal action.

answers.question: Where do PR-1 lines appear?
answers.answer: In a separate patient-responsibility group, not the denial list.

answers.question: Can anyone appeal a PR-1 line?
answers.answer: No role can.

answers.question: Is the patient statement in scope?
answers.answer: No; statements are out of scope for this change.

checks: The PR-1 next action is copied exactly: 'Post the amount to patient responsibility. Do not open an appeal.'
No role has an appeal action on a PR-1 line.
PR-1 lines never appear in the denial list.
Patient statements are listed as out of scope.
Every acceptance criterion's outcome can be observed by a test.
Nothing is presented as agreed that the decisions did not say; any such choice is flagged under open questions as a proposal needing sign-off.
No feature beyond the brief and the decisions (for example an audit log, an override, or a notification) is added unless it is flagged as a proposal.
A PR-1 line on a claim that also has a CO-50 line still offers no appeal on the PR-1 line.

briefs.brief: The front desk must not be able to schedule an imaging visit when the patient's coverage is inactive, and must see why.

answers.question: Which coverage states block scheduling?
answers.answer: Only inactive. Unknown coverage shows a warning but does not block.

answers.question: Can anyone override the block?
answers.answer: No override in this version.

answers.question: Which identifiers can the screen show?
answers.answer: Synthetic PAT-### ids only; no names.

checks: Inactive coverage blocks scheduling and names the reason.
Unknown coverage warns but does not block.
No override path exists for any role.
Only synthetic PAT-### ids appear; no patient names.
The front desk has no denial-workqueue actions.
Nothing is presented as agreed that the decisions did not say; any such choice is flagged under open questions as a proposal needing sign-off.
No feature beyond the brief and the decisions (for example an audit log, an override, or a notification) is added unless it is flagged as a proposal.
A visit already scheduled before coverage became inactive is not handled by this brief and is flagged, not silently decided.

briefs.brief: The PFS lead needs a summary of open lines counted by CARC class, with the number of appealable denials that are already overdue.

answers.question: Which classes are counted?
answers.answer: Denial, patient responsibility, and informational, matching the CARC table classes.

answers.question: Can the lead act on lines from the summary?
answers.answer: No; the summary is read-only.

answers.question: What does overdue mean?
answers.answer: The filing deadline (date of service plus 90 days) has passed.

checks: Counts use exactly the CARC table classes: denial, patient responsibility, informational.
The summary is read-only; the lead has no ready or appeal action from it.
Overdue is defined from the date of service plus 90 days.
Informational (OA-23) lines are not counted as denials.
Every acceptance criterion's outcome can be observed by a test.
Nothing is presented as agreed that the decisions did not say; any such choice is flagged under open questions as a proposal needing sign-off.
No feature beyond the brief and the decisions (for example an audit log, an override, or a notification) is added unless it is flagged as a proposal.
A deadline falling exactly on the demo date counts as 0 days remaining, which is not overdue.

briefs.brief: OA-23 lines must show the prior payer's adjudication and must never be worked as denials.

answers.question: What does the specialist do with an OA-23 line?
answers.answer: Confirms the prior payer adjudication; nothing else.

answers.question: Can an OA-23 line reach the appeal path?
answers.answer: Never.

answers.question: Does it count toward denial totals?
answers.answer: No.

OA-23 lines never reach appeal-ready or any appeal state.

Every acceptance criterion's outcome can be observed by a test.
Nothing is presented as agreed that the decisions did not say; any such choice is flagged under open questions as a proposal needing sign-off.
No feature beyond the brief and the decisions (for example an audit log, an override, or a notification) is added unless it is flagged as a proposal.
OA-23 lines are left out of the denial count but still counted under informational in the summary.

briefs.brief: On CO-4 denials, the biller must correct the procedure modifier before resubmitting, and the product must never suggest or invent a modifier.

answers.question: Who corrects the modifier?
answers.answer: The coder sets it; the biller resubmits.

answers.question: Can the product suggest a modifier?
answers.answer: No, never.

answers.question: Can a CO-4 line be resubmitted unchanged?
answers.answer: No; the modifier must change first.

The coder sets the modifier and the biller resubmits; roles are not mixed.
Every acceptance criterion's outcome can be observed by a test.

No feature beyond the brief and the decisions (for example an audit log, an override, or a notification) is added unless it is flagged as a proposal.
A modifier changed and then changed back to its original value still blocks resubmission.
